fields.name: FieldRequests
fields.evidence: Array with 8-byte elements: bg3.exe+0x1D13E50 drains a request list of 16-byte {EntityHandle, 8-byte value} entries (system +0x800, count +0x80C), gets this component through bg3.exe+0x1D17060 (component +0 of the CommandQueue storage, AllocRaw size 0x20) and appends the 8-byte value with stride 8 (grow FUN_1405c4620, size at +0xC). The destructor bg3.exe+0x6A93D0 frees it without per-element work. The value is most likely an ls::EnumFlags<ecl::character_creation::EDefinitionField> (the macOS command processor keeps a DynamicArray of those, 8-byte stride) - not proven, so written as uint64_t. Live empty.

fields.name: Commands
fields.evidence: Destructor bg3.exe+0x6A93D0 resizes it to 0 with bg3.exe+0x6DACE0: stride 0x70, 16-byte aligned alloc, element destroyed at +8. Element type ecl::character_creation::DefinitionCommand (macOS DynamicArray<DefinitionCommand> stride 0x70 too). Live empty.

summary: Queue of character-editor commands (UI -> DefinitionCommandProcessor::ProcessCommands). situation 'respec' (Osi.StartRespec on the host, then the character editor's commands, level SYS_CC_I); born together with the other ecl::character_creation components of this batch.
open_questions: Meaning of the 8-byte values of FieldRequests (EnumFlags<EDefinitionField> by the macOS hint).
Members inside the DefinitionCommand variant (50 alternatives) - kept as raw storage plus the index byte, as variants are written.
second_pass: The first array was settled on Windows as 8-byte elements (bg3.exe+0x1D13E50 appends the 8-byte value of each queued request through bg3.exe+0x1D17060); the Commands array (stride 0x70, variant at +8, index at +0x68) stands on the Windows destructor bg3.exe+0x6A93D0 / resize bg3.exe+0x6DACE0 read before. Element +0 is an EntityHandle (bg3.exe+0x2035B10 writes the iterated entity there when queuing a portrait command).
live_reason: only empty (all-zero) instances were seen: the member boundaries are untested
